 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 19.03.2011, passed by the tribunal, in MVC No.1988/2009, questioning fastening contributory negligence of 25% on him and also for enhancement of compensation.
2. The factum of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident and coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.
The only disputed fact is whether there is contributory negligence on the part of the claimant or not.

3. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
4.

It is the case of the claimant that on 22.01.2009 at 02.15 p.m. the claimant along with his wife were returning from KLE to Sulebavi on motorcycle NC: 2023:KHC-D:13265 No.KA-22/W-196 and when they reached a place called KLE bypass road, Belagavi, at that time the driver of Maruti Car No.MH-09/AB-8736 drove the car with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the claimant's motorcycle,
due to which the claimant and his wife have sustained injuries.

Therefore,
the claimant has filed the claim petition and the tribunal while awarding compensation has attributed 25% of contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
Further more, in the criminal case the entire negligence is on the part of the driver of car.
Therefore it is submitted that the claimant has not contributed his rashness and negligence.
Hence he prays to fasten the entire rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the car and also prays for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent insurance company submitted that the wife of the claimant who was pillion rider on the motorcycle herself has given statement before the police that her NC: 2023:KHC-D:13265 husband the claimant was riding the motorcycle with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident and therefore charge sheet is filed against both the drivers.

Further submitted that the place of accident is a National Highway and the car was moving from Maharashtra to Andhra Pradesh through National Highway and the claimant was riding the motorcycle to cross the National Highway.

For crossing the National Highway it is bounden duty on the part of the claimant to halt, watch and then proceed, but without following these principles the claimant had driven the motorcycle with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
Therefore, the claimant has also equally contributed negligence and rashness as that of the driver of the Maruti Car.
But however the tribunal has fastened 25% on the claimant.
Hence prays to dismiss the appeal on this ground.
6. Upon considering the scenario of the accident as discussed above, the place of accident is on National Highway.
The claimant was riding the motorcycle and was NC: 2023:KHC-D:13265 coming from a single road to cross the National Highway.

It is duty cast on the claimant while crossing the National Highway to halt for a moment, watch and then proceed after confirming that no movement of vehicles so as to cross the National Highway; but without doing so, he was in the process of crossing the National Highway.
7. On the National Highway the movement of vehicles is normally speed.

Therefore it is also bounden duty on the part of the claimant while crossing the National Highway to halt for a moment,
watch and then proceed to cross the National Highway.
Therefore, in this regard the claimant has also contributed his rashness and negligence to the accident.
The Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against both the claimant and driver of Maruti Car.

8. The wife of the claimant who was pillion rider on the motorcycle has given statement before the police that her husband who is claimant herein has also driven the motorcycle with speed and in a rash and negligent NC: 2023:KHC-D:13265 manner and caused the accident.
The wife is eye witness and based on her statement the charge sheet is filed.
In the charge sheet it is allegation against both the drivers.
Therefore the tribunal is correct in holding the claimant is also responsible for the accident.
Therefore, attribution of 25% of rashness and negligence on the part of the claimant is hereby confirmed.
9. From the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant has suffered following injuries.

3 10. The tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Injury pain and agony.
2. Medical expenses.

3 . Nursing attendant charge extra 10,000  nourishment and conveyance.

Loss of amenities, future 20,000  unhappiness.
Total: 3,21,000  Deduction of 25%: 80,250
Net compensation: 2,40,750  11.
Considering the injuries sustained above discussed, the claimant has suffered three fracture injuries to the right leg.
Therefore a compensation of Rs.75,000/- is awarded under the head injuries, pain and suffering.
The compensation awarded by the tribunal towards medical expenses and hospital charges of Rs.1,40,000/- is as per the actual bills and receipts produced; therefore, the same is kept intact.
12. The accident is caused on 22.01.2009.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, for the accident year 2009, notional income would be Rs.5,000/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimant was aged 50 years old at the time of accident.
Therefore, appropriate applicable NC: 2023:KHC-D:13265 multiplier is 13.
The doctor has given evidence that the claimant has suffered 55% physical disability to the right lower limb.
The tribunal has considered it as 15% to the whole body.
The claimant has suffered three major fractures and one among is comminuted fracture of right femur.
The claimant is a weaver by profession.
The leg requires physical strength for weaving the clothes.
But due to fracture of femur bone and fibula of right leg, then the right leg may not co-operate for weaving work.
Hence to this extent the claimant is constrained to suffer loss of income due to disability and moreover the functional disability considered by the tribunal at 15% is on lesser side.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained as discussed above, it is just and proper to take functional disability at 22% applying the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another,
reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

certainly it affects future prospects in life.

Accordingly as per the age group mentioned in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, and as per the Division Bench judgment of this Court in New India Assurance Company Vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar in MFA No.103807/2016 C/w. MFA Nos.103835/2016 &
103807/2018 and as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram vs.
Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2023) 3 SCC 439, even in the case of injuries, certain income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 19.03.2011, passed by the Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court-III and Addl. MACT, Belagavi, in MVC No.1988/2009, stands modified.
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13265 iii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,70,320/- (75% of Rs.4,93,760/-), along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
iv) The contributory negligence on the part of claimant fixed by the tribunal at 25% is confirmed.
v) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
vi) No order as to costs.

vii) Draw award accordingly.
